SCS uses name-only embeddings as a practical simplification. We validate this choice empirically: name+definition SCS yields equivalent predictive accuracy ($\Delta r$: $-0.023$ to $+0.035$; Appendix~\ref{app:scs-ablation}), and for MAVEN/FewRel prompts that use type names without definitions, name-only SCS directly matches prompt content. We use MiniLM as the primary embedding for BCS computation because sentence-transformers are specifically trained for semantic similarity \cite{sentence-bert-2019}; a cross-embedding sensitivity check using Qwen3-32B causal-LM hidden states confirms directional consistency but with compressed BCS range (std${}\,=\,0.034$ vs.\ MiniLM std${}\,=\,0.081$), consistent with known autoregressive anisotropy \cite{ethayarajh-contextual-2019}.

58	\paragraph{SCS as a lightweight proxy.}
59	\label{sec:scs-validation}

import math
from scipy import stats

# T0-1: MDE sensitivity analysis

# 1. Logit-scale TOST MDE (n=69)
# For TOST: we need the MDE at 80% power
# TOST uses two one-sided t-tests
# For equivalence with margin delta, power = P(reject both one-sided tests)
# The critical approach: MDE is the margin needed for 80% power given n and alpha

# For a paired/one-sample TOST-like test on interaction coefficient
# n=69 observations, alpha=0.05 (each one-sided test)
# Residual SE of interaction from the regression

# From Appendix: interaction = 0.111 logit, 90% CI [0.019, 0.203]
# The 90% CI width = 0.203 - 0.019 = 0.184
# SE = width / (2 * 1.645) ≈ 0.184 / 3.29 ≈ 0.0559
# Alternatively from 95% CI (if available), or from the t-value

# Using the formula: MDE for TOST at 80% power
# MDE ≈ SE * (z_alpha + z_beta) where z_alpha = 1.645 (one-sided 0.05), z_beta = 0.842 (80% power)
# But for TOST, the null is that |effect| >= margin, so:
# Power of TOST = P(t_lower > t_crit AND t_upper < -t_crit)
# Approximate MDE: margin where power = 0.80

# SE of interaction coefficient in logit scale
# From 90% CI: [0.019, 0.203], point estimate 0.111
# 90% CI uses t_{n-p-1, 0.05} ≈ t_{65, 0.05}
t_crit_90 = stats.t.ppf(0.95, df=65)
se_logit = (0.203 - 0.019) / (2 * t_crit_90)
print(f"SE of logit interaction: {se_logit:.4f}")

# For TOST, MDE at 80% power:
# margin = point_estimate + SE * (t_alpha + t_beta)
# where we need: P(reject H0: |theta| >= margin) = 0.80
# Assuming true effect = point_estimate = 0.111
# MDE ≈ |theta_0| + SE * (z_alpha + z_beta)
# Actually, for the TOST to have 80% power, the margin must be:
# margin >= |observed_effect| + SE * (t_alpha,df + t_beta_inv)
z_alpha = stats.norm.ppf(0.95)  # 1.645
z_beta = stats.norm.ppf(0.80)   # 0.842
mde_logit = abs(0.111) + se_logit * (z_alpha + z_beta)
print(f"MDE for 80% power (logit): {mde_logit:.3f} logit")

# Convert to pp at median accuracy (0.65 -> logit = 0.619)
# d(logit)/d(p) = 1/(p*(1-p)), so dp ≈ dlogit * p*(1-p)
p_median = 0.65
mde_pp_median = mde_logit * p_median * (1 - p_median)
p_floor = 0.51
mde_pp_floor = mde_logit * p_floor * (1 - p_floor)
print(f"MDE at median p={p_median}: ~{mde_pp_median:.1f} pp")
print(f"MDE at floor p={p_floor}: ~{mde_pp_floor:.1f} pp")

# Our margin is ±3 pp → logit margin at p=0.51: 3pp/(0.51*0.49) = 0.120 logit
# At p=0.65: 3pp/(0.65*0.35) = 0.132 logit
# The paper says ±0.156 logit
logit_margin_051 = 0.03 / (0.51 * 0.49)
logit_margin_065 = 0.03 / (0.65 * 0.35)
print(f"\n±3pp margin in logit at p=0.51: {logit_margin_051:.3f}")
print(f"±3pp margin in logit at p=0.65: {logit_margin_065:.3f}")
print(f"Paper uses ±0.156 logit (at median accuracy)")

print(f"\nConclusion: MDE ~{mde_logit:.2f} logit > margin 0.156 logit")
print(f"So the logit TOST is underpowered (margin < MDE), explaining p=0.209")

# 2. NER batch-level null (n=450)
# MDE for correlation at 80% power
# For detecting r at alpha=0.05 (two-tailed), power=0.80
# n = 450
# Using the formula: r_min = sqrt(chi2_ncp / (chi2_ncp + n - 2))
# Or approximation: r_min ≈ (z_alpha + z_beta) / sqrt(n - 3)
z_alpha_2 = stats.norm.ppf(0.975)  # 1.96 (two-tailed)
z_beta_1 = stats.norm.ppf(0.80)     # 0.842
mde_r = (z_alpha_2 + z_beta_1) / math.sqrt(450 - 3)
print(f"\nNER batch-level MDE (n=450): r = {mde_r:.3f}")
print(f"Observed r ≈ 0.004, well below MDE")
print(f"Power at r=0.09: >80%, so null is well-powered")

PYEOF
